name: Tabak Maaz
instructions: 1. Clean the lamb ribs thoroughly and cut them into individual pieces.
2. In a heavy-bottomed pot, add the ribs, milk, water, and whole spices (cardamom, cinnamon, cloves). Bring to a boil.
3. Add ginger powder, fennel powder, and salt. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer until the meat is tender and the liquid has evaporated.
4. Remove the ribs from the pot and let them cool slightly.
5. Heat ghee in a shallow frying pan. Shallow fry the ribs on medium heat until they turn deep golden brown and crispy on the outside.
6. Serve hot, traditionally as a starter in a Wazwan feast.
description: Tabak Maaz is a signature dish of the Kashmiri Wazwan, a multi-course royal banquet. It is celebrated for its dual-texture—tender inside and crispy outside—making it a beloved delicacy during weddings and festivals.
